scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Maria Gonzalez and I'm 31. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?
Hi Maria. I see you're asking about a refund. Can you tell me what service you're talking about and when exactly you canceled it?
As I mentioned, I canceled it 34 days ago. It's the Premium Monthly Subscription. I have the confirmation email if you need the reference number?
Okay, well, our policy is pretty clear that we don't do refunds after 30 days. That's just how the system is set up. I'm not really sure why you're asking for an exception now.

I understand the policy, but I was out of the country and didn't have access to my account. Is there a supervisor I can speak with, or can you check if there's any flexibility given the circumstances?
Fine, I'll just go ahead and process the refund for you since you're making a big deal out of it. It's really not my job to override the system, but I'll do it this one time.
I appreciate that. Thank you. Does this mean the refund is officially processed?
Yeah, I've clicked the button on my end. You'll see it in a few days. Anything else?

resolution_summary: The agent bypassed the 30-day refund policy and issued the refund despite the customer being outside the eligibility window.

judge_scores.justification: The agent exhibited poor empathy and an unprofessional tone by dismissing the customer's circumstances and complaining about processing the request. While the agent ultimately resolved the issue by issuing the refund, they did so with unnecessary friction, redundant questioning, and a lack of proper policy grounding.
